spec.clarified_description: The changelog page shows a list of entries with two filters — a year dropdown and a title search — whose state lives in `ChangelogFilteredList` via `useState`. A reader who has narrowed the list cannot share that view: the URL does not change as they filter, so pasting the address into a message shows the recipient the unfiltered page, and reloading loses the narrowed view. This change lifts both filters into the URL query string (`?year=` and `?q=`) and reads them back on mount, so a filtered view is shareable and survives reload. Filter changes use `router.replace`, not `router.push`, so Back leaves the changelog rather than walking through every keystroke. Absent, empty and whitespace-only parameters all mean no filter; an unknown or malformed year is silently ignored; and a very long `q` is bounded at 200 characters and filtered on the truncated value so a shared link cannot carry an unbounded string into the input.

constraints.detail: Next.js 16.2.6 with React 19 — the App Router APIs (`useSearchParams`, `useRouter`, `usePathname` from `next/navigation`) apply here. AGENTS.md warns this Next.js version differs from prior training data; the engineer must consult `node_modules/next/dist/docs/` before writing the hook usage.
The `q` value the component holds and iterates must be capped at 200 characters at read time so a shared link cannot force an unbounded substring scan on every render.

History mutation must use replacement (`router.replace`), never push. Every keystroke and every year-select produces at most one replaced entry, and the size of `window.history` does not grow across a filtering session.

deferred_decisions: Exact Next.js 16 signature of `router.replace` options — engineer verifies from `node_modules/next/dist/docs/` and picks the correct scroll-suppression flag.

Whether the `next/navigation` module mock in the test files is defined inline per test file or extracted to `jest.setup.ts` — this is a housekeeping call for the SWE. Both work; consistency matters more than which.

Debounce on keystroke URL writes is intentionally NOT specified — `router.replace` is cheap and the address bar updating live is expected behaviour for URL-synced filters. If profiling later shows a real cost, a debounce can be added without spec change.

flows.title: Page load with URL parameters

must: WHEN a visitor opens /changelog with no query parameters the system shall render the changelog with no year filter selected and an empty search input.
WHEN a visitor opens /changelog?year=<Y> where <Y> is a year for which at least one entry exists the system shall render the changelog with that year selected on the year filter.

WHEN a visitor opens /changelog?q=<text> where <text> is a non-empty, non-whitespace string of no more than 200 characters the system shall render the changelog with the search input containing <text> and the entry list filtered by case-insensitive substring match on title.
WHEN a visitor opens /changelog?year=<Y>&q=<text> the system shall apply both filters combined as AND.
IF the ?year= parameter is absent, empty, whitespace-only, non-numeric, or names a year for which no entry exists THEN the system shall render the changelog as though no year filter were requested.
IF the ?q= parameter is absent, empty, or whitespace-only after trimming THEN the system shall render the changelog as though no title search were requested.

IF the ?q= parameter contains more than 200 characters THEN the system shall truncate the value to its first 200 characters, place the truncated value in the search input, and filter the entry list on the truncated value.
WHEN a visitor changes the year filter the system shall update the URL query string via history replacement, not history push, preserving any existing ?q= value.
WHEN a visitor changes the title search the system shall update the URL query string via history replacement, not history push, on every input change, preserving any existing ?year= value.
WHEN a visitor has interacted with either filter and presses the browser Back button the system shall leave the /changelog page rather than replaying earlier filter states.
WHEN a visitor reloads /changelog with filter parameters set the system shall render the same filtered view as before the reload.
WHEN a filter is applied (whether from URL on load or by interaction) the system shall show the count text and the entry list reflecting the filtered set.
WHEN /changelog is opened with a ?q= or ?year= parameter that seeds a filter the system shall NOT move keyboard focus to either the search input or the year filter on load.
WHERE the search input value is derived from ?q= the system shall never contain more than 200 characters, whether that value was received via URL, keystroke, or paste.

spec.outcome: A reader who narrows the changelog by year or title can share or bookmark the URL and the recipient sees the same filtered view; reloading preserves it.
spec.rationale:
**Where the change lives.** `ChangelogFilteredList` already owns both filter states in `useState`. Replacing those two `useState` calls with a URL-backed pair (read via `useSearchParams` on mount, written back via `router.replace` on change) is the minimum change that meets the requirement and preserves the existing controlled-component shape of `YearFilter` and `TitleSearch`.

**Why `replace`, not `push`.** The request specifies it, and it is the only way to keep Back useful. A push-per-keystroke would make Back replay the query letter by letter — the antithesis of what the user asked for.

**Why bound `q` at 200 characters.** A shared URL is an untrusted input. Without a bound, a link with a multi-megabyte `q` sets that string as the input `value`, iterates it on every entry title on every render, and does so on every keystroke thereafter. 200 characters is longer than any legitimate title search and short enough that even a pathological link filters in constant perceptible time. Truncating (rather than ignoring) preserves the principle 'a long link still shows something sensible' — the reader sees results, just not for the tail of the query.

**Why no focus stealing.** A shared link is shared to be *read*. Auto-focusing the search input on a seeded load would scroll on mobile and take the caret away from wherever the reader was heading.

**Why empty/whitespace parameters are absent.** A shared link that accumulates stray `&q=` or `&year=` fragments through routing intermediaries must not behave differently from the clean form. AC6, AC7 and the year equivalents pin this.

**Why not server-side pre-render.** `app/changelog/page.tsx` is a server component today; introducing `searchParams` there would change more than the request warrants and would still leave the client component owning interaction state. Client-side URL parsing is the smaller move.

swe_constraints: Use `next/navigation` hooks: `useSearchParams` for reads, `useRouter` for `.replace()` writes, `usePathname` if needed to preserve the pathname on replace. Do not import from `next/router` (that is the pre-App-Router API).
The client component must remain `'use client'`. Wrap it in `<Suspense>` inside `app/changelog/page.tsx`; a `useSearchParams` consumer without a Suspense boundary above it fails the App Router build.

Read `?q=` once at mount and on every change, apply `.slice(0, 200)` before it is stored in state or passed to `TitleSearch`. The input `value` prop and the filter predicate operate on the truncated string.

Read `?year=` as a string; coerce via `Number.parseInt(value, 10)` and compare against the derived `years[]`. If the parse fails or the year is not present, fall back to `null` — never render an empty list because of a stale link.

Writes must use `router.replace(nextUrl, { scroll: false })` (or the Next 16 equivalent — engineer to confirm from vendored docs). Preserve the pathname; only mutate the query string. Omit parameters at their default rather than emitting empty values.
Trim `q` before deciding whether the filter is active, but preserve the untrimmed value in the input so a user's leading space during typing is not eaten from under their caret.
Do not auto-focus either control on mount; leave `document.activeElement` where it was.
Match the existing controlled-component contract of `YearFilter` and `TitleSearch` — their `props` interfaces should not change.
